observed_vs_expected: The pre-declaration expected distinct convergence behavior and stopband improvement. Instead, best_target_score began at 0.922720 (round 1) and closed at 0.921129 (round 7), failing to surpass its own peak despite seven executions. The score sequence [0.9227, 0.7961, 0.0196, 0.4406, 0.7425, 0.4927, 0.9211] shows extreme volatility rather than smooth convergence. tightest_margin recorded at 0.492629 provides no clear monotonic improvement signal, indicating the asymmetry hypothesis has not yet manifestly succeeded over the symmetric baseline.
deviation_mechanism: Layers indexed 8 through 17 are universally pinned at the hard constraint boundary of 215.0 nm across all evaluated candidates. This boundary clamping creates a structurally rigid central spacer that decouples the phase accumulation of the top and bottom Bragg stacks. Because the optimizer cannot adjust the mid-stack thicknesses, the remaining outer layers (indices 0–7 and 18–19) are forced into aggressive, compensatory excursions to satisfy the global objective, producing highly non-smooth gradients. This parameter stiffening causes the transfer matrix calculations to sample deeply mismatched quarter-wave regimes, explaining the catastrophic score drop to 0.019643 when compensatory overshoot peaked.
continue_rationale: Seventeen rounds have not been executed (only 7), but the current trajectory clearly identifies a solvable structural issue rather than algorithmic exhaustion. The route recovered from its minimum score (0.019643) back to 0.921129, proving the design space contains valid high-performance configurations. The persistent boundary pinching is a fixable constraint-handling failure, not a physical impossibility. Continuing with reduced dimensionality will yield scientifically valuable data on whether asymmetric tuning actually improves stopband margins once the optimization manifold is de-stiffened.
